newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND EYES BANK PEKAO PUBLIC OFFERING H1 1998.
newsitem.headline: POLAND EYES BANK PEKAO PUBLIC OFFERING H1 1998.

text.p: The first stage of the privatisation of Poland's Bank Pekao SA group will be a public offering of five to 15 percent of the group's shares in the first half of 1998, a deputy finance minister said on Tuesday.

"The government has accepted the proposal and affirmed (the group's) privatisation...The first stage of the privatisation, a public offering of five to 15 percent of the bank, will take place in 1998's first half," Karol Szwarc said.
Szwarc told a news conference after a cabinet meeting that the government saw the group worth three to 4.5 billion zlotys.
He said that employees would retain up to 15 percent of the group's shares and 30 percent would go in the reform of the country's social security system currently underway.

Szwarc said that after a second stage of the privatisation, in which up to 30 percent of shares would be sold along with a likely capital raise, more than 51 percent of the group's shares would be in private hands.
He did not say when the second stage would take place and said the privatisation programme did not envision a strategic investor for the group, but that "several stable investors" could take shares.
Pekao president Andrzej Dorosz, also present, said the government would announce a tender for an adviser to the privatisation in the next few weeks.

The Bank Pekao SA group formed last year after the state treasury lumped together with Bank Pekao SA Pomorski Bank Kredytowy W Szczecinie SA (PBKS), Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy SA (PGS) and Bank Depozytowo-Kredytowy SA (BDK).
The group expects to make a pre-tax profit of more than a billion zlotys this year against 848.4 million last year. Its net profit last year was at 243.4 million zlotys.
The group's balance sheet total last year was at 41.6 billion zlotys and own funds 1.9 billion zlotys.
